title: Profile and optimize vector429 Round2
objective: Profile vector429 p=2 through the shared native Round2 resource and materially reduce its dominant general kernel or route it through a bounded exact selector without fixture-specific logic

oracles: ordinary Python Round2 exact local HNF
forced original exact native multiplier and basis transformations
exceptions: Bounded optimization of the existing audited FLINT/GMP Round2 representation primitive; no new mathematical algorithm

handoff.summary: General sparse radical storage, exact hash deduplication, p-squared modular reuse, signed power-of-two limb reduction, and sparse fmpz basis fast paths reduce vector429 p=2 Round-2 from 19.398s to 11.802s and vector010 p=2 from 0.906s to 0.585s. Both high-degree payloads match the forced exact implementation byte-for-byte; focused randomized and sanitizer checks pass.
risks: The remaining vector429 floor is the 169-bit exact fmpz tensor basis transform (81.4% of Round-2 time); closing the PARI gap requires a separately proved representation change rather than another bounded host cleanup.
The audited header metrics are intentionally not edited in this distribution lane, so central integration must refresh architecture/native-audit.json before architecture:check.
next_steps: Update the number_field_order_ffi.h audit metrics from 1309 lines/53642 bytes to 1410 lines/58164 bytes and extend its existing storage rationale, then run pnpm architecture:check.
Retain the current generic native-first word-prime selector: vector010 p=2 native is 45.3x faster than forced Round-4 while forced polygon and OM each exceed 30 seconds.
Run the full native/platform validation suite from the integration lane; Windows continues to use the exact tested fallback where the optimized host capability is unavailable.
